samples.xml_description:
<module id="sequence_detector">
    <description>Detects a specific 4-bit binary sequence 1001 using a sequential logic block and an FSM.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronization.</input>
        <input id="reset_n">Asynchronous reset signal to initialize the state machine.</input>
        <input id="data_in">1-bit input signal representing the current bit of the sequence being detected.</input>
        <output id="sequence_detected">1-bit output signal indicating whether the specific sequence has been detected.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="IDLE">Waiting for the start of the sequence.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S1">The first bit of the desired sequence is detected.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S2">The second bit of the desired sequence is detected.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S3">The third bit of the desired sequence is detected.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S4">The fourth and final bit of the desired sequence is detected, setting the output sequence_detected high.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="current_state">Sequential register to hold the current state of the state machine.</reg>
        <reg id="next_state">Sequential register to hold the next state of the state machine.</reg>
        
        <always @(posedge clk or posedge reset_n)> // Sequential logic block triggered on positive edge of clk or reset_n
            if (reset_n == 1'b1) begin
                current_state <= IDLE; // Initialize current_state to IDLE state when reset_n is high
            end else begin
                current_state <= next_state; // Update current_state with next_state value on each clock cycle
            end
        </always>
        
        <always @(*)> // Combinational logic block to determine the next state based on current_state and data_in
            case(current_state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b1) begin
                        next_state = S1; // Transition to S1 state if data_in is 1
                    end else begin
                        next_state = IDLE; // Stay in IDLE state if data_in is not 1
                    end
                end
                
                S1: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b0) begin
                        next_state = S2; // Transition to S2 state if data_in is 0
                    end else begin
                        next_state = S1; // Stay in S1 state if data_in is not 0
                    end
                end
                
                S2: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b0) begin
                        next_state = S3; // Transition to S3 state if data_in is 0
                    end else begin
                        next_state = S1; // Stay in S1 state if data_in is not 0
                    end
                end
                
                S3: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b1) begin
                        next_state = S4; // Transition to S4 state if data_in is 1
                    end else begin
                        next_state = IDLE; // Go back to IDLE state if data_in is not 1
                    end
                end
                
                default: next_state = IDLE; // Default case to handle unexpected states
            endcase
        </always>
        
        <assign sequence_detected = (current_state == S4); // Assign output signal sequence_detected based on current_state
        
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>Implements a sequence detector using a sequential logic block and an FSM to detect the specific sequence 1001.</implementation>
</module>
